intro: Word for insurance agents on Mac is the regular Word for Mac app, pointed at the jobs that repeat every week. Those jobs are client letters, renewal notices, quote cover notes and certificate requests. Build a template for each one, then check mail merge before you send a bulk email to clients. Lazur, a voice assistant for the Mac, can point at menus and guide you while you work.
tldr: Store each recurring letter and form as a template with File > Save as Template, using .dotx unless the file has macros.
Mail merge to email on Mac needs Outlook as your default mail app, or Merge to E-Mail stays grayed out.
Word for Mac does not add a different attachment to each recipient during a merge, so plan that step first.
Ask Lazur where a control sits, or to guide you one click at a time, while you work in Word.

blocks.text: Most agents do not write long documents in Word. They fill in the same few documents again and again, and each one goes to someone who is waiting for it. That makes Word for Mac a tool for repeat work. The gain is not fancy formatting. The gain is a template that already has your agency wording, your signature block and the right blanks, so each new document takes minutes.

The Mac version of Word is close to the Windows version, but several menu names differ. A few features also behave differently. This page points out the gaps now, so you find them before a client is waiting.
Build Word for Mac templates for the letters you send every week

Start with the document you rewrite most often. For many agents that is a renewal letter, a certificate of insurance request, a quote cover note or a claim status update. Open a clean copy of the finished version, not a file you already sent to a client. Delete the client name, policy number and dates. Replace each one with a bracketed placeholder, such as [Insured name] or [Effective date]. The brackets show what to fill in before the document leaves your desk.

To save the master, go to File > Save as Template. Set File Format to Microsoft Word template (.dotx). Use Microsoft Word Macro-Enabled template (.dotm) only when the document contains macros. A plain letter has no macros, so .dotx is the right choice for most agency documents. To use the template later, go to File > New from Template and pick it. Word opens a new copy, so the master stays clean. The full steps are in [how to create a template in Word on Mac](/how-to/create-a-template-in-word).

items: Write the request once in a clean document.
Replace every client detail with a bracketed placeholder.
Add one line at the top that lists what to check before sending.
Choose File > Save as Template, then pick Microsoft Word template (.dotx).
Name the file by document type and year, such as Certificate request 2026.
Open every new document from File > New from Template, never from the master.

blocks.title: Keep one master per document type
blocks.text: Keep a separate master for each document type. If you change a template for one client, save that as a new file with the client name in it. A master should never hold a client name, a policy number or a premium.
Mail merge email on Mac has one big catch

Mail merge sends the same email to many people, with each person's name and details filled in. In Word for Mac, start it at Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Email Messages. Microsoft's guide lists this path for Mac. Windows uses different wording, such as E-mail Messages. When your list and email text are ready, send the batch with Mailings > Finish & Merge > Merge to E-Mail.

Here is the catch. Microsoft's guide says Merge to E-Mail is unavailable if you have not selected your default email program. A Microsoft Q&A thread from 2024 gives the same answer. Mac Word needs Outlook set as the default email program for mail merge to email. If the option is grayed out, check that setting first. In Apple Mail, open Mail > Settings and set Outlook as the default mail client. Return to Word. If the button is still gray, save the document and restart Word.

If your agency does not use Outlook, the built-in merge email path will not fit your setup. Plan a different route before you build the list. You can still merge the letter text in Word, then copy each finished letter into the email app you use. That is slower, but it works for a short list of clients.

blocks.text: Per-recipient attachments do not work in a Mac merge

This is where many agents get stuck. A Microsoft Community Support Specialist wrote in June 2025 that Word for Mac does not support adding attachments during a mail merge, the way some Windows versions do. Microsoft's own guide describes an attachment option for the merge format. That option attaches the Word document itself, and the email has no body text. These two sources describe different things, so test before you rely on either.
Here are the workarounds people use, as listed in the Microsoft Q&A thread.

items: After the merge, drag each file into the matching message in Outlook's Outbox or Drafts.
Use a third-party mail merge tool such as GMass, Mailchimp or Mailmeteor. Check each tool's pricing page before you sign up.
For a few clients with unique files, send those emails one at a time from your mail app.

blocks.text: Here is a worked case. Say you send renewal notices to a list of clients, and each client has a different PDF. Build the merge for the text and the addresses. Send one test to yourself with one attachment added by hand. Only then drag the files into the real drafts. The test shows whether each file lands in the right message, before a client sees it.
How much time Word and AI tools save insurance agents

Read these figures as direction, not measurement. Liberty Mutual's 2026 Independent Agency Growth Study, as reported by IA Magazine, covered nearly 1,200 U.S. independent agency principals and staff. Weekly AI use rose from 18% to 41% in the same study. The findings cover AI in general, not Word.
Users in that coverage report an average saving of four hours a week, and 14% say they saved eight or more. Both numbers are self-reported. Nobody checked them against a timer.

Renegade Insurance cites an Agency Revolution survey from 2026. It says 54% of agencies spend more than half of each week on manual, repetitive tasks. The sample size is not stated. The article itself warns that no neutral body measures this. Treat that number as a direction too.

For your own week, the useful question is narrower. Which Word job repeats most? A template that saves a few minutes on each letter adds up faster than any survey average. Start with that job, time it for a week, and decide from your own numbers.
Ask Lazur while you work in Word

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘, which is Option and Command together, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. You do the clicking. Lazur does not click or edit for you.

blocks.title: Client data and AI tools
blocks.text: Check your agency's rules before any AI tool sees client data. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Dictate file notes and proposal text without retyping

Typing a file note after a client call often takes longer than the call. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor, in Word or any other app. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Add carrier names, underwriter names and endorsement terms to the personal dictionary once. After that, dictated text spells them the way you set them.

blocks.title: Read dictated text before it leaves
blocks.text: Dictation is fast, and it still makes mistakes. Read every name, number, date and policy term before the text goes to a client. A wrong policy number is easy to miss on screen, and it causes a second email.
Format long proposals with heading styles

Headings make a proposal easier to check and easier to send. Select the line that starts a section. Then go to Home > Styles and pick Heading 1 for the main section or Heading 2 for a subsection. On a Mac keyboard, ⌃⌥1 applies Heading 1 to the current paragraph. Headings also feed the navigation pane, which you can open from View > Navigation Pane. Click any heading there to jump to it. Use the same styles in every template, so the same map works across documents. The step-by-step version is in [how to apply heading styles in Word on Mac](/how-to/apply-heading-styles-in-word).
Review changes from clients, underwriters and your team

Turn on Track Changes before you send a draft out. Go to Review > Track Changes, then turn it on. Every edit shows up in color, with the author name. Use Review > New Comment to ask a question about one line without changing the text. When the draft comes back, accept changes one at a time, so a single bad edit does not slip through.

Compare two versions when a marked-up copy arrives from another party. The compare tool lists each difference, so you can confirm that only the coverage changes you asked for made it in. The full steps are in [how to compare two documents in Word on Mac](/how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word).

items: Track Changes is off, or every change has been accepted or rejected on purpose.

The file name matches the document type and the client.

blocks.text: Mistakes agents make in Word on Mac

items: Saving a template with a client name still in it. Search the master for names before you save.
Saving the master as a regular .docx file, which turns it into a normal document you can overwrite by accident.
Trusting an email merge without a test send to yourself first.
Following a Windows tutorial step by step. Menu names differ on Mac.
Blaming the template when the real problem is the default mail app setting.

blocks.text: Two habits prevent most of these. Reopen the master after saving, and send one test merge before the real batch. Those checks take minutes, and they catch the errors that cause the most rework.
Your first week with Word for Mac

Pick one document you send every week and build its template. Check your Word build under Word > About Word. Microsoft lists Word for Mac 16.114.4 (26110224), released November 4, 2026, so you can compare your build against it. Then try a mail merge with a short list of people you know, and send yourself the test first.

If Merge to E-Mail is grayed out, fix the default mail app first. If clients need a different file in each email, plan the workaround before the send day, not on it. Ask Lazur to point at the menus while you do this. You can compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing), and get the app from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Can Word for Mac send a mail merge as email?
faq.answer: Yes, but the send step depends on your default mail app. Start at Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Email Messages. Microsoft's guide says Merge to E-Mail is unavailable until you select your default email program, and the Microsoft Q&A answer names Outlook.

faq.question: Why is Merge to E-Mail grayed out in Word on Mac?
faq.answer: Usually the default mail app is not set to Outlook. In Apple Mail, open Mail > Settings and set Outlook as the default mail client. Then return to Word. If the option is still gray, save the document and restart Word.

faq.question: Can I attach a different file to each recipient in a Word mail merge on Mac?
faq.answer: Not during the merge, according to a Microsoft Community Support Specialist. Merge the text first, then drag each file into the matching message in Outlook's Outbox or Drafts. Send one test message before the real batch.

faq.question: Should I save my insurance template as .dotx or .dotm?
faq.answer: Use .dotx for almost every letter, form or request. Choose .dotm only when the document contains macros. Microsoft's template guide lists both options under File > Save as Template.

faq.question: Does Lazur fill in my Word documents or click through menus for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, explains, answers out loud, guides you one click at a time and drafts text. You do the clicking and the editing. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Word or any other app.

faq.question: Is client data safe if I use Lazur while I work in Word?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Check your agency's rules before you use any AI tool with client data.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows for Word users?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Which Word for Mac build should I check for these steps?
faq.answer: Go to Word > About Word and compare your build with Microsoft's update history. Microsoft lists 16.114.4 (26110224), released November 4, 2026. Menu names can shift between builds, so follow the guide that matches your screen.
